title: Sensor limbo & alert wildfire analysis — oncall notes + runbook draft
content:
Summary:

Short: On 2025-02-09 we saw a rapid surge of SLO burn alerts originating from tail-latency rules plus a large flood of 'missing_metric' alerts tied to the telemetry exporter. The two cascaded into an alert wildfire that overloaded the on-call and paging pipeline. This doc captures the on-call timeline, triage, temporary mitigations we used, and a proposed runbook/longer-term fixes.

Why unique: this incident wasn’t a single backend failure — it was a coupling between partial metric scrape failures (exporter-level) and tight SLO alert windows which made transient gaps look like systemic latency regressions. Alerts amplified each other (pager -> human -> config churn) and obscured the minimally invasive fix.

Incident timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-09 03:12 UTC: First drop in telemetry exporter 'model_serving/kv_cache_hits' observed in Prometheus (metric sparsity).
- 03:14 UTC: Missing-metric alert (prod-exporter-scrape-gap) fires; Pager to SRE team (escalation policy A).
- 03:15–03:18 UTC: Multiple SLO tail-latency rules (p95/p99 tail windows) start burning; our on-call Slack floods.
- 03:20 UTC: Engineer restarts the telemetry exporter on one shard (temporary relief for a subset of metrics).
- 03:22 UTC: Alerts rebound and spread to other services — downstream inference gateways report elevated request queue depth and bursty CPU.
- 03:35 UTC: We apply a temporary alert mute (1 hour) on lower-priority missing-metric rules to stop paging noise.
- 04:10 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis centers on exporter OOM + scrape backlog + new label cardinality introduced by a recent release of model tagging (see REDWOOD-1987).
- 05:00 UTC: Alerting hysteresis PR created to add 3m for missing-metric rules and 30s smoothing for tail-latency; follow-ups assigned.

Symptoms we observed (concrete):
- Metric groups with new label combinations (model:variant, region) increased series cardinality ~5x for exporter-metrics over a short window.
- Prometheus scrape durations spiked (prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds 95th jumped from 200ms -> 8s).
- Remote_write backpressure increased, write queue length grew on the ingest side.
- Several exporters experienced brief OOMs and restarted, causing ephemeral metric gaps.
- SLOs configured with short window and no debounce treated gaps as latency regressions (we were using p99 over 5m with immediate firing).
- Alert fatigue: responders muted alerting channels manually which delayed detection of an independent infra issue 30 minutes later.

Immediate mitigations we executed (what worked, in order):
1) Stop-the-bleed: add temporary 1-hour mute on missing-metric page policy (pager escalation to notify-only) to reduce human load while we triage. NOTE: only mute non-critical rules; do not mute SLA-critical network or disk alerts.
2) Restarted exporter pods/shards showing OOM and rotated them to newer node pools with slightly higher mem; this recovered several missing series.
3) Reapplied Prometheus scrape config fallback: reduced label relabeling for high-cardinality metrics (rolled-back an earlier experiment); decreased scrape duration.
4) Throttled alerting on SLO tail rules by triggering them only if the missing-metric alert persisted for >3m (temporary rule override).
5) Opened hotfix PR to remove the buggy label emission in model tagging code (PR link in linked artifacts).

Root cause (working hypothesis):
- A change in our model tagging pipeline (deployed ~03:00 UTC) introduced high-cardinality labels to the telemetry exporter for inference requests. That increased scrape payload size. Combined with an exporter memory regression and Prometheus remote_write backlog, some exporter shards OOMed sporadically, producing metric gaps. Our alert rules treated missing/empty series as TTL-broken signals and some SLO rules with short windows flagged tail-latency as broken. The conflation of metric-loss + tight SLO windows created the alert cascade.

Runbook draft: how to handle next time (structured steps)
- Detection:
  * Primary signals: prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds (95p spike), exporter_restart_count increase, prometheus_remote_write_queue_length, 'missing_metric' rule firing.
  * Secondary signals: KV cache hit/drop, request_queue_depth, node_memory_utilization.
- Immediate actions (0–10 minutes):
  1. If missing_metric alerts are >5 concurrent and scrape_duration 95p > 2s, set missing-metric escalation to 'notify-only' for 30–60m (do not mute SLA-critical alerts).
  2. Identify top-3 exporters with highest restart_count / longest last_scrape_duration and restart pods sequentially (avoid mass restarts).
  3. Check Git deploys in last 30m for telemetry/exporter changes (git log + deployment tags). Open REDWOOD ticket if needed.
- Short term (10–60 minutes):
  1. Temporarily increase alert firing thresholds for tail-latency SLOs by applying smoothing window (e.g., require p99>threshold for 3 consecutive evaluations OR add 30s exponential smoothing).
  2. Run diagnostic PromQL queries (examples below) and attach to incident ticket.
  3. If exporter OOM suspected, cordon the node and migrate exporter pods to the experimental 'telemetry-bigmem' pool.
- Post-incident (owner + 72h):
  1. Roll out PR that removes the high-cardinality label emission and add unit test to guard cardinality.
  2. Add a permanent alert that triggers if label-cardinality increases > 2x in 1h for critical exporters.
  3. Update documentation: 'telemetry cardinality change checklist' in Confluence.

PromQL snippets to run during triage (copy/paste):
- Top exporters by scrape duration:
  topk(10, prometheus_scrape_duration_seconds{job=~"exporter.*"})
- Exporter restart spikes (10m window):
  increase(process_start_time_seconds_count{job=~"exporter.*"}[10m])
- Label cardinality estimate (approx):
  count(count by (model_variant) (inference_request_count{job=~"exporter.*"}))
- Remote_write backpressure:
  prometheus_remote_write_queue_length

Proposed alerting rule changes (short list):
- missing-metric rules: add 3m sustained window and annotate which rules are pager-critical.
- tail-latency SLOs: require 2 consecutive evaluations or add 30s smoothing.
- add a new 'cardinality-jump' rule for exporters: fires at >2x unique series increase in 1h.
- add circuit-breaker policy: when exporter restart_count > X in Y, mute low-priority alerts and escalate to infra pager.

Longer-term improvements and experiments:
- Telemetry pipeline: add automatic series cardinality guardrails and CI check for any new label emission in telemetry PRs.
- Build a synthetic heartbeat service per region that writes a small, known metric every 10s; flag if missing for >90s (less noisy than entire exporter missing-metric).
- Introduce alert-mapping metadata: every rule must declare 'is_pager_critical' and a suggested debounce.
- Trial: implement 'alert-rescorer' that lowers priority of alerts when many upstream missing_metric signals are active (to reduce wildfires).

Owners and next steps (who does what):
- Telemetry hotfix (remove label): Samir Patel (owner) — PR created; target deploy 2025-02-12.
- Prometheus config rollback + relabeling: Riley Novak (owner) — schedule canary 2025-02-11.
- Runbook & alert rule changes: SRE-ops squad — Jules Ortega to draft PR to Alertmanager rules 2025-02-14.
- Postmortem + exec summary: Avery Chen to write and circulate (due 2025-02-16).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want the synthetic heartbeat metric to be unique per exporter or per region? Tradeoff: many heartbeats increase series count; one per region might not localize failures.
- How aggressive should automatic mute policies be? (risk: hide real infra issues).
- Are there other services that recently added label fields around the same time? Search deploy history.

Notes to self / on-call shorthand (quick checklist):
- If pager noise > 10 pages in 5m, stop and evaluate for missing_metric cascade (don’t restart everything at once).
- Prefer sequential restarts and moving pods to bigger nodes before mass config changes.
- Always attach Prometheus query outputs to incident ticket; include grafana snapshots.

Appendix: links referenced during triage
- REDWOOD-1987: model-tagging high-cardinality incident ticket (root-cause tracked)
- telemetry-config PR #42: revert relabeling experiment
- Confluence: telemetry cardinality checklist (draft)

End of notes.

(Informal / scratchpad style — lots of TODOs and fragments above; use as working runbook and refine into a final playbook after the postmortem.)
